newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UNCERTAINTY PREVAILS ON BELGIAN OLO MARKET.
newsitem.headline: UNCERTAINTY PREVAILS ON BELGIAN OLO MARKET.

text.p: Worries over the future of EMU following France's Left victory in Sunday's elections and a German gold revaluation row will remain the talk of the town at the Brussels bond market this week, traders said.

Bonds recovered from early weakness in cautious late afternoon trade on Monday in line with Bunds but traders expected the rebound to steady levels to be shortlived as markets were increasingly worried that EMU would be weakened by the entry of countries like Italy and Spain.
"With the prospect of a weaker-than-expected euro, people will increasingly sell Europe against the U.S." one trader said.
Traders said they were puzzled by the lack of reaction on French financial markets to the clear victory of the Left in the French poll despite the fact it had been largely discounted.
"It's just incredible that it doesn't affect the franc, Pibor (Paris Interbank Offered Rate) or long term," one said. "A few years ago a Left win would still have sparked a slide," he said.
He said Europe already underperformed the U.S. last week.
Banque Degroof said in its weekly comment that the strength of the future euro would be questioned more and more and that uncertainty would prevail.
Degroof said they expected range-trading and low volumes in current circumstances with volatility coming from reactions to rumours and guidance provided by Bunds and T-bonds.
It said it expected monthly U.S. jobs data on Friday to be the main market mover as players would be looking for clues as to whether the U.S. economy was growing.
"Most likely, T-bonds will be steady and Europe will continue lagging," Banque Degroof said.
One trader said he expected the yield on the 30-year T-bond to rise to above seven percent again in the near term.
